correctness.rationale: For image sets E,F, the ordered product has image e(F∩dom e). Shared roots contribute h deterministically, and the s−h marked nonroots must hit exactly t−h additional roots. Counting assignments by inclusion–exclusion gives the first formula; alternatively restrict selected elements to those mapped to a chosen set of allowed roots or left undefined, then extract the coefficient of selected-set size by inclusion–exclusion. Both count the choices outside F and the (s+1)^(n−s) idempotents with image F. Partial identities realize each admissible intersection, including zero and n=0. At fixed ranks the root sets are independent uniform subsets, so the hypergeometric variance is O(n) and H/n→ab. Conditional on H the remaining independent choices change occupancy by at most one apiece, giving uniform concentration (m=0 is deterministic). The unattained-root probability is (1−1/(r+1))^(s−H), which yields the stated limit and the two unequal values. Direct composition tested 299,755 ordered pairs through n=5, including the swapped histograms (0,800,5950)/(0,1080,5670). An independent occupancy recursion and polynomial multiplication matched for 5,440 admissible-range triples through n=14. Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/replay_3_4_5.py 5. These tests corroborate the finite identities, not the limiting proof.

value.rationale: Product-image rank is a natural invariant of the semigroup and the all-rank census identifies both the complete feasible range and an exact computable law beyond one-factor enumeration. The same statistic shows a macroscopic order effect for independent fixed-rank factors: swapping densities changes the positive limiting fraction, so orientation is not just a rare finite-size pathology. These are useful finite and asymptotic facts about arbitrary partial idempotents; no novelty is assigned to inclusion–exclusion itself.
